title: General Galois Formula via IsCyclotomicExtension: Module Overview
content: This entry answers the open question from AngleTrisectionCos20GalOQ01OQ02: yes, IsCyclotomicExtension is sufficient to prove the general formula |Gal(minpoly(cos(π/n))/ℚ)| = φ(2n)/2 for all n ≥ 3. The Lean file is structured in 6 sections: (1) the cosine identity, (2) the degree theorem (sorry-free), (3) extension degree (sorry-free), (4) splitting field degree (1 sorry), (5) Galois order, and (6) consistency checks. The header identifies the key reduction: cos(π/n) = cos(2π/(2n)), which allows the cos(2π/m) machinery from AngleTrisectionOQ02OQ03OQ01 to be applied with m = 2n.
mathContext: $\mathbb{Q}(\cos(\pi/n)) = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{2n})^+$ (maximal real subfield of $n$-th cyclotomic field). $[\mathbb{Q}(\cos(\pi/n)):\mathbb{Q}] = \varphi(2n)/2$. Galois group: $(\mathbb{Z}/2n\mathbb{Z})^\times / \{\pm 1\}$ of order $\varphi(2n)/2$. For $n=5$: degree 2 (cos(36°) satisfies a quadratic). For $n=7$: degree 3 (cos(π/7) is a root of a cubic). For $n=9$: degree 3.

title: The Central Reduction: cos(π/n) = cos(2π/(2n))
content: The lemma cos_pi_eq_cos_2pi_div_2n proves cos(π/n) = cos(2π/(2n)) by `congr 1; push_cast; ring`. This is arithmetically trivial (π/n = 2π/(2n)) but mathematically decisive: it reduces the cos(π/n) problem to the cos(2π/m) problem with m = 2n, which is exactly what AngleTrisectionOQ02OQ03OQ01 formalizes. The entire proof of the degree theorem flows from this single identity. The `NeZero (2*n)` instance is needed downstream to satisfy cyclotomic field infrastructure requirements.
mathContext: $\cos(\pi/n) = \cos(2\pi/(2n))$ since $\pi/n = 2\pi/(2n)$. After `congr 1`, the goal is $\pi/n = 2\pi/(2n)$; `push_cast` handles the coercions $n : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$; `ring` closes. The cosine value at $2\pi/(2n)$ is exactly $\text{alphaCos}(2n)$ in the notation of AngleTrisectionOQ02OQ03OQ01.

title: Degree Theorem (Sorry-Free): natDegree = φ(2n)/2
content: cos_pi_minpoly_natDegree is the main mathematical result, proved with 0 sorries. The proof chain: (1) `haveI : NeZero (2*n) := ⟨by omega⟩` to enable cyclotomic field instances; (2) `rw [cos_pi_eq_cos_2pi_div_2n]` to rewrite as cos(2π/(2n)); (3) `rw [← minpoly_alphaCos_eq_minpoly_cos]` to transfer to the alphaCos element; (4) `exact minpoly_alphaCos_natDegree` from AngleTrisectionOQ02OQ03OQ01. The entire mathematical content is in the parent file — this theorem is a direct corollary via the cosine identity.
mathContext: `natDegree(minpoly ℚ (\cos(\pi/n))) = \varphi(2n)/2`. The key parent lemmas: `minpoly_alphaCos_eq_minpoly_cos (m : ℕ)`: minpoly ℚ (alphaCos m) = minpoly ℚ (Real.cos (2π/m)). `minpoly_alphaCos_natDegree (m : ℕ)`: natDegree(minpoly ℚ (alphaCos m)) = φ(m)/2. Applying these with m = 2n and using the cosine identity gives the result.

title: The One Sorry: Normality of ℚ(cos(π/n)) over ℚ
content: The splitting field degree sorry requires showing that ℚ(cos(π/n)) = SplittingField(minpoly(cos(π/n))). The mathematical argument: (1) ℚ(cos(π/n)) is Galois over ℚ (it is the fixed field of conjSubgroup = ⟨complex conjugation⟩ in the abelian Galois group (ℤ/2nℤ)×, and every subgroup of an abelian group is normal, so the fixed field is Galois over ℚ by the fundamental theorem of Galois theory); (2) Galois extensions have the property that every element's minimal polynomial splits completely over the extension; (3) ℚ(cos(π/n)) is generated by one root of minpoly(cos(π/n)), so SplittingField = ℚ(cos(π/n)). Lean 4 formalization requires about 80 additional lines of intermediate field and Galois correspondence lemmas.
mathContext: **Key step**: conjSubgroup $\leq (\mathbb{Z}/2n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ (generated by $k \mapsto -k$) is normal since the Galois group is abelian. By Galois correspondence: $\text{Fix}(\text{conjSubgroup}) = \mathbb{Q}(\cos(2\pi/(2n))) = \mathbb{Q}(\cos(\pi/n))$ is Galois over $\mathbb{Q}$. Galois $\Rightarrow$ SplittingField(minpoly) = $\mathbb{Q}(\cos(\pi/n))$.

title: Cross-Checking Against Known Cases
content: The consistency check section verifies the general formula φ(2n)/2 against three previously proved specific cases. n=5: φ(10)/2 = 4/2 = 2 matches the degree-2 result for cos(36°) = (1+√5)/4 proved in AngleTrisectionCos20GalOQ01OQ02. n=7: φ(14)/2 = 6/2 = 3 matches the degree-3 result proved in AngleTrisectionCos20GalOQ01. n=9: φ(18)/2 = 6/2 = 3 matches the degree-3 result proved in AngleTrisectionCos20Gal. These checks serve two purposes: (1) mathematical confidence that the formula is correct, (2) testing that the general theorem specializes correctly.
mathContext: Euler's totient: $\varphi(2n) = \varphi(2)\varphi(n) = \varphi(n)$ when $n$ is odd, and $\varphi(2n) = 2\varphi(n)$ when $n$ is even (for $n \geq 3$). Specifically: $\varphi(10) = 4$ (units of $\mathbb{Z}/10\mathbb{Z}$: $\{1,3,7,9\}$); $\varphi(14) = 6$ ($\{1,3,5,9,11,13\}$); $\varphi(18) = 6$ ($\{1,5,7,11,13,17\}$). Each halved: 2, 3, 3.
